metadata.title: Conditional Density Lift and Dual-Witness Xi Functional
metadata.description:
Abstract

A nonzero real vector can be mapped to a unit vector by taking signed square roots of its normalized absolute coordinates. The associated rank-one projector retains relative magnitudes and signs while forgetting total mass and common sign. We apply this construction to an optimal residual and an optimal dual witness for a finite-dimensional minimum-distance problem in the sum norm. Their trace distance defines an alignment statistic. Complementary slackness gives a strict upper bound below one for every optimal pair, and characterizes the zero-distance case. Successive coordinate minimization selects a unique pair once a coordinate order is fixed. The construction is undefined at a zero residual; a separate convention assigns the statistic the value zero there. We give proofs, an explicit example, and a selection policy that uses the statistic only after primary residual comparisons. The accompanying numerical implementation and discrete Lean results have distinct, stated scopes.

Why This Matters

The paper distinguishes what its diagnostic inequalities measure from stronger claims that do not follow. Explicit definitions and counterexamples make the selection policy and its limits inspectable.

Core Theorems

The numbered propositions and proofs in the manuscript state their domains and hypotheses. The revision separates quotient residuals, input norms, discrete formal lemmas and numerical evaluations rather than treating them as equivalent.

Formal Verification and Computational Artifacts

The package includes source code, tests, a pinned standalone Lean project, an explicit declaration census and source-bound rendered files. The quick start gives commands for replay. Each formal result retains the scope described in the manuscript; test outcomes do not supply a theorem beyond that scope.

Scope Boundaries and Non-Claims

The real projector construction and strict primal-dual distance bound have prose proofs. Lean checks discrete integer and rational statements. Numerical vector evaluation does not establish optimality or compute the canonical selector.

Reproduction

See [quick_start.md](quick_start.md) for installation, tests, the Lean census, rendering and independent archive checks. The manuscript and documentation use CC-BY-4.0; reference software and tests use MIT. The renderer, Lua filter and path helper
retain Apache-2.0; see the component table in README.md.

Related Identifiers and Citations

Verified scholarly sources are listed in [references.md](references.md).
The new revision has no assigned DOI. The previous record is [10.5281/zenodo.20192297](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20192297); its verified parent is [10.5281/zenodo.20192296](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20192296). The metadata records these version relationships.
